findings.evidence: Kinematics.lean:92 `def xi (i : Invariants) : ℝ := i.Dq / i.Pq`; Kinematics.lean:212-215 docstring: "The argument `xi` is the light-cone momentum fraction `Δ⁺/P⁺` ... at finite energy the target-elastic boundary is not exactly `tMinElastic M (Invariants.xi i)`"; Kinematics.lean:242-243 `theorem Invariants.t_le_tMinElastic_iff (i : Invariants) (M xi : ℝ)`. Roadmap Convention 1 (Diffraction/README.md:111) names this exact trap: "a file in which two different momentum fractions are both called `x` and a lemma about one is applied to the other".
findings.fix: Rename the light-cone argument throughout to a distinct name (e.g. `xiLC`, with the declarations becoming `tMinElastic M xiLC`, `tMinElastic_xiLC_zero`, etc.), or state the boundary in terms of the invariant `Invariants.xi` so one `xi` means one thing. Note `ExclKinematics.xiSkew` already takes the disambiguating-suffix route for the third ξ-like variable (Exclusive/Kinematics/Basic.lean:92).
findings.issue: `tMinElastic (M xi : ℝ)` names its second argument `xi`, but its docstring (lines 212-215) states this `xi` is the light-cone fraction `Δ⁺/P⁺`, which "agrees with the invariant `ξ = Δ·q / P·q` of `Invariants.xi` only up to relative corrections of order `Q²M²/(P·q)²`" — i.e. a different quantity from `Diffractive.Invariants.xi` (line 92) in the same namespace, with no lemma relating them. Nothing in the API signals the difference, so `tMinElastic_nonpos M (Invariants.xi i)` elaborates and reads as the physical boundary while, per the author, it is not. Same identifier reused at lines 234 (`tMinElastic_def`), 237 (`neg_tMinElastic`), 248 (`tMinElastic_xi_zero`), 255 (`tMinElastic_nonpos`), and worst at line 242, where `Invariants.t_le_tMinElastic_iff (i : Invariants) (M xi : ℝ)` puts both meanings in one signature: `i.xi` and the free `xi` are different ξ's.

summary: Names and suffixes otherwise match the roadmap's prescribed vocabulary and the statements they carry, and no notation is introduced. But `xi` is used for two inequivalent quantities in one namespace — `Invariants.xi` (the invariant `Δ·q/P·q`) and the argument of `tMinElastic` (the light-cone `Δ⁺/P⁺`), which the file's own docstring says are not equal at finite energy.
